recipes.name: Plain Steamed Rice

steps.text: Rinse the rice 3 times until the water runs clear, then soak for 15 minutes.
Bring 330 ml water to a boil in a pot, add the drained rice and a pinch of salt.
Cover and cook on the lowest flame until all the water is absorbed.
Switch off and rest covered, then fluff gently with a fork.

tips: Measure cooked rice with a bowl (about 3/4 cup per serving) to keep portions consistent.
Cooled and reheated rice has more resistant starch, which is gentle on blood sugar.

recipes.name: Kerala Red Matta Rice

steps.text: Rinse the red rice well and soak for at least 30 minutes.
Pressure cook with 4 cups water and salt for 5 whistles, then let pressure release naturally.
Drain excess starchy water through a colander and fluff the grains.

tips: Matta rice keeps you fuller than white rice thanks to its bran layer.
Cook a big batch; it keeps 3 days refrigerated.
recipes.makeAhead: Soak overnight to cut cooking time by a third.

recipes.name: Jowar Roti

steps.text: Bring 150 ml water with salt to a boil, take off heat and stir in the jowar flour; cover and rest.
Knead the warm dough with wet hands until smooth and crack-free, then divide into 6 balls.
Pat each ball into a thin round on a floured board, rotating as you press.
Cook on a hot tawa, brushing the top with water; flip and cook the second side until spotted.
Puff briefly over direct flame and brush lightly with ghee before serving.

tips: Hot-water kneading makes gluten-free jowar dough much easier to roll.
2 rotis per serving pair well with chicken or mutton curry.
recipes.makeAhead: Cooked rotis keep 1 day wrapped in a cloth; reheat on tawa.

recipes.name: Instant Ragi Dosa

steps.text: Whisk ragi flour, rice flour, lactose-free curd and about 350 ml water into a thin, lump-free batter.
Stir in cumin, chopped chilli, curry leaves, spring onion greens and salt; rest the batter.
Heat a tawa until very hot, then pour batter from the edges inward like a rava dosa, leaving lacy holes.
Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges and cook until crisp and releasing from the pan.
Fold without flipping and serve immediately.

tips: Ragi is rich in calcium and fibre; keep it to about 30 g per serving for comfortable digestion.
Stir the batter before every dosa as the flour settles.

recipes.name: Small Whole-Wheat Phulka

steps.text: Mix atta and salt with about 65 ml warm water into a soft dough; cover and rest.
Divide into 8 small balls and roll each into a thin 13 cm circle.
Cook on a hot tawa until bubbles appear, flip and cook briefly.
Puff over direct flame with tongs and brush very lightly with ghee.

tips: Each serving is 2 small phulkas (25 g atta) to stay within the wheat fructan limit for IBS.
Try sourdough-style long resting (overnight in fridge) to make wheat easier to tolerate.
recipes.makeAhead: Knead dough the night before and refrigerate in a closed box.

recipes.name: Quinoa Vegetable Pulao

steps.text: Rinse quinoa thoroughly in a fine sieve to remove bitterness.
Heat ghee and garlic oil, crackle cumin and whole spices, add hing and grated ginger.
Add diced carrot, beans and capsicum and sauté until slightly tender.
Add quinoa, salt and 300 ml water; bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low.
Rest covered, fluff and finish with chopped coriander.

tips: Quinoa adds complete protein, making this a great base for lighter fish meals.

recipes.name: Lemon Rice

steps.text: Cook the rice so grains stay separate, spread on a plate and cool.
Heat oil, fry peanuts until golden, then add mustard seeds, red chilli, curry leaves, slit green chilli and ginger.
Add hing and turmeric, switch off the flame and pour in the lemon juice.
Fold the cooled rice and salt into the tempering gently without breaking grains.

tips: Add lemon juice off the heat to keep it fresh and avoid bitterness.
Travels well in a lunch box.

recipes.name: Neer Dosa

steps.text: Blend rice flour, grated coconut, salt and 400 ml water into a very thin, watery batter.
Heat a non-stick tawa and grease lightly with coconut oil.
Pour a ladle of batter from the edge, swirling the pan so it spreads thin, then cover.
Cook without flipping until the edges lift and the dosa looks set; fold into quarters.

tips: Stir the batter every time – the flour sinks quickly.
Classic pairing with Mangalorean chicken or fish curry.

recipes.name: Light Poha

steps.text: Rinse poha in a colander for a few seconds, drain and rest so it softens.
Heat oil, fry peanuts, then add mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chilli, hing and turmeric.
Add grated carrot and peas and cook covered until tender.
Add poha and salt, toss gently and steam covered on low.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander.

tips: Spring onion greens replace onion here to keep it low-FODMAP.

recipes.name: Beans Poriyal with Coconut

steps.text: Finely chop the beans and carrot.
Heat coconut oil, splutter mustard seeds, add red chilli, curry leaves, hing and turmeric.
Add vegetables, salt and a splash of water; cover and cook until just tender.
Stir in grated coconut and cook uncovered for a minute.

tips: Do not overcook – beans should stay bright green with a slight bite.

recipes.name: Cabbage Carrot Thoran

steps.text: Shred cabbage and grate carrot finely.
Crush coconut, green chilli and turmeric together coarsely.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in coconut oil, add vegetables and salt; cook covered.
Add the coconut mix, toss and cook uncovered until dry.

tips: Keep cabbage to about 75 g per serving for IBS comfort; carrot bulks it up.

recipes.name: Spinach Stir Fry

steps.text: Wash spinach thoroughly and chop roughly.
Heat garlic oil, add cumin and broken red chilli.
Add spinach and salt, stir fry on high until wilted.
Sprinkle coconut and serve.

tips: Spinach is a great iron and folate source – pair with a squeeze of lemon for better absorption.

recipes.name: Bottle Gourd Kootu

steps.text: Pressure cook moong dal with turmeric and water for 2 whistles.
Cook diced bottle gourd with salt and a little water until soft.
Grind coconut, cumin and green chilli into a paste; add with the dal to the gourd and simmer.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves and hing in oil and pour over.

tips: Moong dal is kept under 20 g per serving to stay low-FODMAP.

recipes.name: Ridge Gourd Curry

steps.text: Peel ridges of the gourd and dice; chop tomato.
Temper mustard, cumin and curry leaves in oil; add ginger and hing.
Add tomato and spice powders; cook until soft.
Add ridge gourd and salt, cover and cook in its own juices until tender.
Garnish with coriander.

tips: Ridge gourd releases plenty of water – no need to add any.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Bhindi Kurkure

steps.text: Wash and fully dry the okra, then slice lengthwise into thin strips.
Toss with spices, salt, lemon juice and oil, then dust with rice flour and cornflour.
Air fry at 180°C in a single layer, shaking the basket halfway.
Finish 2 minutes at 200°C for extra crunch and serve immediately.

tips: Dry okra completely before slicing to avoid sliminess.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Baingan Bharta

steps.text: Prick the brinjal all over, rub with a few drops of oil and air fry at 200°C, turning halfway, until skin is charred and flesh collapses.
Cool slightly, peel and mash the flesh.
Heat oils, add cumin, ginger and green chilli, then tomatoes and spice powders; cook until soft.
Add mashed brinjal and salt, cook 3 minutes, finish with spring onion greens and coriander.

tips: A tiny drop of mustard oil gives the smoky Punjabi flavour.

recipes.name: Capsicum Tomato Sabzi

steps.text: Cube the capsicum and chop tomatoes.
Heat oil, add cumin and hing, then capsicum; stir fry on high until blistered.
Add tomatoes, spice powders and salt; cook until tomatoes break down.
Crush kasuri methi over and mix.

tips: Use mixed red and green capsicum for more vitamin C and colour.

recipes.name: Cucumber Tomato Kachumber

steps.text: Dice cucumber, tomato and carrot finely.
Toss with chopped spring onion greens, coriander, chilli and toasted cumin powder.
Dress with lemon juice, olive oil and salt just before serving.

tips: Salt right before serving so it stays crunchy.

recipes.name: Cucumber Raita

steps.text: Whisk lactose-free curd until smooth.
Grate cucumber, squeeze lightly, and add to the curd.
Season with roasted cumin powder, pepper, salt and chopped mint and coriander; chill.

tips: Lactose-free curd keeps this raita IBS-friendly while adding protein.

recipes.name: Bengali Pumpkin Sabzi

steps.text: Peel and dice pumpkin into small cubes.
Heat oil, add fenugreek, fennel, cumin and hing (a quick panch phoron), then ginger.
Add pumpkin, tomato, spice powders and salt; cover and cook on low, stirring occasionally.
Mash lightly, add jaggery and lemon juice and cook 2 minutes.

tips: Pumpkin is rich in beta-carotene; leave some cubes whole for texture.

recipes.name: Broccoli Carrot Stir Fry

steps.text: Cut broccoli into small florets and carrot into thin batons.
Blanch broccoli in boiling water, then drain.
Heat oils in a pan, add ginger, then carrot and broccoli; toss on high heat.
Add soy sauce, pepper and salt, finish with spring onion greens and sesame seeds.

tips: Keep broccoli to florets – the stalks are higher in FODMAPs.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Paneer Tikka

steps.text: Whisk lactose-free curd with ginger, spices, lemon juice, half the oil and salt.
Coat paneer cubes, capsicum and tomato chunks; marinate.
Arrange in the air fryer basket without overlapping and brush with remaining oil.
Air fry at 200°C, flipping halfway, until charred at the edges.
Squeeze over a little extra lemon juice and serve hot.

tips: Pat paneer dry before marinating so the coating sticks.

recipes.name: Paneer Bhurji

steps.text: Crumble paneer coarsely.
Heat ghee, add cumin, ginger and chilli, then capsicum and tomato; cook until soft.
Add spice powders and salt, then the paneer; toss gently.
Finish with spring onion greens and coriander.

tips: Add paneer last and cook briefly so it stays soft.

recipes.name: Light Palak Paneer

steps.text: Blanch spinach, then plunge into iced water.
Blend spinach with green chilli and ginger into a smooth puree.
Heat ghee and garlic oil, add cumin, tomato and garam masala; cook until soft.
Add puree, salt and lactose-free milk; simmer gently.
Whisk in curd off the heat, add paneer cubes and kasuri methi; warm through.

tips: Ice-water shocking keeps the gravy vivid green.

recipes.name: Tofu Bhurji

steps.text: Press tofu to remove water and crumble.
Heat oil, add cumin, ginger and chilli, then capsicum and tomato.
Add tofu, turmeric, garam masala, pepper and salt; stir fry until dry.
Finish with spring onion greens and coriander.

tips: Use firm tofu – it is naturally low-FODMAP, unlike silken.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chilli Paneer

steps.text: Toss paneer cubes with half the cornflour, pepper and salt; spray lightly with oil.
Air fry at 200°C, shaking halfway, until golden.
Heat garlic and sesame oil, stir fry ginger, chilli and capsicum on high.
Add sauces, vinegar and remaining cornflour mixed with 60 ml water; simmer until glossy.
Toss in paneer and spring onion greens and serve.

tips: Swap paneer with 300 g firm tofu for a lighter vegan version.

recipes.name: Paneer Capsicum Skewers

steps.text: Soak wooden skewers in water.
Mix curd, ginger, spices, lemon juice, oil and salt; coat paneer, capsicum and tomato.
Thread alternately onto skewers.
Air fry at 190°C, turning the skewers halfway, until charred.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size as the paneer for even cooking.

recipes.name: Kadai Paneer

steps.text: Dry roast red chillies, cumin and coriander, then coarsely grind into kadai masala.
Heat ghee and garlic oil, add ginger and pureed tomato; cook until oil separates.
Add capsicum chunks and kadai masala; cook on high so capsicum stays crisp.
Fold in paneer, kasuri methi and spring onion greens; simmer briefly.

tips: Freshly ground kadai masala is the secret – no onion needed.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats with Chia and Kiwi

steps.text: Combine oats, chia seeds, lactose-free milk, curd and grated jaggery in a jar.
Stir well, close and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, stir and top with diced kiwi and papaya.

tips: Kiwi helps with regularity in IBS-C.
recipes.makeAhead: Prepare up to 2 days ahead; add fruit fresh.

recipes.name: Whey Banana Protein Smoothie

steps.text: Add lactose-free milk, sliced firm banana, oats and peanuts to the blender.
Blend until smooth, then add whey and pulse just to combine.
Serve chilled.

tips: Use a firm, just-yellow banana – ripe bananas are high in fructans.

recipes.name: Roasted Peanut Chaat

steps.text: Dry roast peanuts until fragrant and lightly cool.
Chop cucumber, tomato and grate carrot.
Toss everything with lemon juice, spices, chilli and salt and serve immediately.

tips: Keep peanuts to about 30 g per serving – a palmful.

recipes.name: Low-FODMAP Fruit Bowl

steps.text: Peel and dice all fruits into bite-sized pieces.
Toss with lemon juice, chopped mint, pepper and a pinch of salt.
Chill briefly before serving.

tips: Avoid apple and mango (high FODMAP) – these fruits are within safe portions.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Masala Peanut and Pumpkin Seed Mix

steps.text: Toss peanuts and pumpkin seeds with oil, lemon juice, spices and salt.
Air fry at 160°C, shaking every 3 minutes, until crunchy.
Add curry leaves and air fry until crisp.
Cool fully before storing in an airtight jar.

tips: Pre-portion into 35 g bags so snacking stays controlled.
recipes.makeAhead: Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight jar.

recipes.name: Ragi Porridge

steps.text: Whisk ragi flour into 200 ml cold water until lump-free.
Cook on medium, stirring constantly, until thick and glossy.
Add lactose-free milk, jaggery and a pinch of cardamom; simmer.
Top with chopped walnuts.

tips: For a savoury version skip jaggery and add buttermilk made from lactose-free curd.
